name: The Linux Foundation
subcategory: 'foundation of foundations' hosting open-source projects (501(c)(6) trade association)
origin_detail: Formed in 2007 by the merger of two industry consortia founded in 2000, Open Source Development Labs (OSDL) and the Free Standards Group, to support Linux. Now an umbrella for sub-foundations (CNCF, PyTorch Foundation, OpenSSF, LF AI & Data, LF Energy, Agentic AI Foundation and others), with a separate 501(c)(3) arm, LF Charities.
openness_notes: Neutral host for OSI-licensed projects with their own governance; funded by corporate membership. Note its legal form: a 501(c)(6) business league 'created for the improvement of business conditions', so donations are not tax-deductible (LF Charities is the 501(c)(3) arm).
latest_value_type: annual revenue, IRS Form 990, fiscal year ending Dec 2024 (expenses $204,369,300; net assets $144.6M)
risk_events: Dependence on corporate membership and events; priorities are set by member companies (business-league status).
Rapid expansion into AI governance: Agentic AI Foundation (9 Dec 2025), React Foundation intent (7 Oct 2025, from Meta), Tokenomics Foundation (4 Aug 2026), Jupyter Foundation (19 Nov 2024).
robustness: Very high: revenue grew from $177.1M (2022) to $196.0M (2023) to $220.7M (2024) with surpluses each year; more than 1,000 corporate members and more than 1,000 hosted projects (per Wikipedia, 2025). Projects are legally separated into sub-foundations.
physical_science_relevance: Indirect but growing: hosts the PyTorch Foundation (the dominant AI framework used in scientific ML), LF Energy, and, through LF Charities, Project Jupyter. Its agentic-AI standards (MCP) are already used to connect AI agents to lab and data tools.
openness_effect_assessment: The Linux Foundation shows open source monetised collectively: companies pay for neutral governance of shared code, which has made it the default home when AI firms open up standards (Anthropic's MCP, OpenAI's AGENTS.md, Block's goose in Dec 2025). Openness here strengthens member companies' ecosystems; it is not a public-science funding model.
key_takeaway: With $221M revenue (2024), the Linux Foundation dwarfs the science-relevant open foundations in this group (NumFOCUS $8.4M in 2024; the ASF $2.2M in FY2025; the RCSB PDB's federal award is about $49M over five years). In 2024-2026 it absorbed AI-era projects (PyTorch, Jupyter, MCP), so corporate-funded foundations, not science agencies, increasingly govern the open tools that AI-for-science depends on.
